transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just feel really restless, like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to sit still. It happens in the radiology suite and in class. I’ve tried to just tough it out for months, but I still end up pacing, shifting around, or making up some reason to get up and move.
Did this restless feeling start after you began taking an antidepressant or after the dose was changed?
I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear connection like that that I’ve noticed.
When you feel restless, do you also get a strong urge to pick at your skin?
Not really, no. I mean, I don’t think I get an urge to pick at my skin when I’m restless. It’s more just… feeling like I need to move.
Since childhood, have you often had trouble staying seated when you were expected to sit still?

Yeah, that’s been a problem for me. Whenever I’m expected to just sit still, like in class or in the radiology suite, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll try to tough it out, but I usually end up shifting around, pacing, or coming up with some excuse to get up and move.
Since childhood, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying focused?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t thought about it much in terms of since childhood. I mean, I know I get restless, but the paying attention part… I’d have to think about that more.
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble keeping your attention on schoolwork or other tasks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really remember it clearly enough from when I was a kid to say whether that was a regular problem or not. I know I had issues sitting still, but with attention on schoolwork specifically… I’d have to think about it more.
When you feel restless, do you also feel anxious or worried?
I’m not really sure. I don’t always think of it as anxiety or worry. It’s more like I just feel physically wound up and need to move. I’d have to pay more attention to whether worry is part of it.
When this happens, do you feel an inner sense of restlessness that gets better when you move?

Yeah, I do. It feels like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to sit still, like in the radiology suite or in class. If I get up and pace, shift around, or find some reason to move, it eases up a bit. I’ve tried to just tough it out for months, but I still end up needing to move.
Did this restless feeling begin soon after you started an antidepressant or after the dose was increased?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember it starting right after a medication change or anything like that. I haven’t noticed a clear connection with an antidepressant or a dose increase.
Are you currently taking an antidepressant?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think so, but I’d have to check the names of what I’m taking to be sure.
Can you check whether you are taking an antidepressant?
I can check, yeah. I don’t have the list in front of me right now, so I’m not sure offhand. If I pull up my meds or look at the bottle names, I can tell you.
Are you taking sertraline, fluoxetine, escitalopram, venlafaxine, bupropion, or any other antidepressant right now?
I’m not sure. None of those names sound familiar off the top of my head, but I’d need to check the bottles or my medication list to say for sure.
When you feel restless, are you also worrying a lot?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed if it’s tied to worrying, exactly. Sometimes I’m just restless, but I’d have to think about whether worry is part of it.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge even when you are not trying to sit still?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as anxiety most of the time. I can feel kind of keyed up, but I haven’t noticed if I’m actually worried or on edge when I’m not trying to sit still.
When you are sitting still and this feeling starts, do you feel afraid that something bad might happen?
I don’t think so. It doesn’t usually feel like fear that something bad is going to happen. It’s more just... I can’t sit still, but I’m not sure there’s a scary thought behind it.
Do you feel this same need to move even when you are free to move around?

Yeah, I do. Even when I’m able to move around, I’m usually still kind of looking for the next thing to do. Most days I go from class to clinicals to the gym or errands, and if I have a gap, I’ll fill it with something because just sitting around feels really hard.
Do you currently have trouble staying focused on tasks?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I get restless, but with focus specifically… I haven’t paid close enough attention to say. It depends on the task, I guess.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on tasks you need to do?
I’m not really sure if I’d say often. I know some tasks are harder to stick with, but I haven’t really tracked whether it’s an attention problem or just me getting restless.
After you check your medication list, are you taking any antidepressant right now?
I’m not sure off the top of my head. I’d have to actually look at the list to say for sure.
Are you taking an antidepressant right now?
I still don’t know for sure. I’d need to check my medication list before I say yes or no.
